title: How to Direct Dial Their Hearts
coreMove: Replace missing face-to-face cues on the phone with warmer voice timing, name use, respectful openings, and message shape.
sourcePressure: Phone-presence unit covering techniques 60 through 70: vocal warmth, using the other person name, honoring interruptions and context, voicemail, openings, pacing, and replacing missing visual cues.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is phone etiquette. The useful version is engineering presence when the other person cannot see your face, hands, or patience.

hook: Use their name on the call
counterintuition: The phone is more intimate than face to face
A good opening solves the call

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine radio dispatcher coordinating with a harbor pilot during dense fog
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatcher whose clipped voice can raise risk under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a pilot hears respect and precision while visibility drops
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before giving the channel change, she says the pilot vessel name slowly, waits for the static to clear, and lowers her pace on the bearing number
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a green radio display flickering beside a fogged harbor window

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice volunteer leaving a voicemail for a family caregiver
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer who must sound human without demanding a callback
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a drained caregiver feels supported rather than tasked
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she rewrites the voicemail to start with the caregiver immediate context, offers one concrete drop-off window, and removes the guilt-laden call me back
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a voicemail script written on the back of a pharmacy receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: a court clerk calling jurors about a postponed reporting time
exampleSpecs.audience: a clerk making repetitive calls that still need individual respect
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether jurors understand the change and stop flooding the office with repeat calls
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the rushed first call with the revised one where she confirms the juror name, pauses after the new time, and gives the parking instruction only after comprehension
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of juror postcards beside a blinking phone console

exampleSpecs.domain: a radio pledge-drive producer calling a major donor between live segments
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer who has twelve minutes and cannot sound transactional
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a donor renews because the station remembers why he gives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: with the countdown clock running, she chooses to open with the donor favorite late-night jazz block before naming the pledge amount
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red on-air light glowing above a donor card

exampleSpecs.domain: a rural veterinary triage line handling a lambing-season call
exampleSpecs.audience: a technician replacing visual reassurance with pace and sequence
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a panicked farmer follows instructions before the vet arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the technician says the farmer name, repeats the one observable sign, and breaks the next action into a single sentence before asking for more details
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a mud-smeared triage notebook open beside a wall phone

exampleSpecs.domain: a piano tuner calling a concert hall manager about a last-minute schedule change
exampleSpecs.audience: a contractor whose request interrupts a packed rehearsal day
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he preserves trust while asking for access to the stage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after one abrupt failed call, he opens the second by naming the rehearsal block he is trying not to disturb, then gives two access windows
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tuning fork lying on a printed rehearsal grid

skillTargets: choose openings that honor phone interruption context
use names and pacing without sounding scripted
shape voicemail so it recognizes the recipient burden
diagnose what visual cue must be replaced by voice or structure

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next call or voicemail, write the other person current context in five words, then open with a sentence that proves you know you are entering that context.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter
